disclaimers.aiPlans: AI helps draft plans and pick swaps — and it can get things wrong. Review every plan, recipe and swap against your own dietary needs and health before you rely on it.
disclaimers.enginePlans: Plan generation and swaps run on a deterministic engine — fast and reproducible, but still review every result against your own dietary needs and health. After an ingredient swap the recipe text is adjusted by plain replacement: it may read awkwardly, and a step that names the old ingredient by another word still names it. The ingredient list is the one to follow.

landing.headline: Meal planning that actually adds up.
landing.subhead: Calorie-targeted plans, deterministic nutrition and shopping lists that write themselves. AI optional — never required.

features.controlBody: Control your diet and its settings: one of eight diets or your own macro split, two to five meals a day, the pace you lose weight at or a calorie target of your own. Rule out allergens and ingredients, lean towards the cuisines you like and give a single day its own target. Adjust it all your way.
features.plansBody: Plans of one day to four weeks that hit your calorie target, laid out on a calendar. The planner leans towards using up what it opens, so less goes to waste, and you can fill chosen days with a favourite set of meals.
features.swapsBody: Swap a meal for another, or an ingredient for one with the same calories, and see what it does to the macros. Make a day, a few days or the whole plan again and keep what you have already eaten.
features.listsBody: A shopping list made from your plan, merged, grouped by aisle and counted the way you shop: eggs in pieces, with the packs each row takes. What your pantry holds is taken off.
features.nutritionBody: Every calorie and macro comes from a curated ingredient database and is worked out by a deterministic engine: the same inputs always give the same numbers, never invented ones.
features.aiTitle: AI only if you want it
features.aiBody: The model your server offers, where its administrator has set one up, or your own OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenRouter or Ollama key. A model may draft a recipe from known ingredients and order the planner's proposals, but never writes a number. Everything works without it.

section1.title: What this is
section1.body:
Diet App is a self-hosted meal-planning application. The operator of this instance is responsible for its uptime, your data, and any service guarantees they choose to offer.

The software is Diet App by White Ravens, with its original source code at https://github.com/whiteravens20/diet-app. It is free software under the GNU Affero General Public License, version 3: anyone may share and change it on the terms of that licence, whose text is in the LICENSE file of the source code. It comes with no warranty of any kind. If this instance runs a changed version, the licence requires its operator to offer you the source code of that version.

section2.title: Accounts
section2.body: Creating an account requires an email address and a password you keep secret. You are responsible for keeping your credentials safe. Account deletion is permanent: when you delete your account the operator hard-deletes every row tied to it — profiles, meal plans, favourites, inventory, AI usage logs — with no recovery path.

section3.title: BYOK keys and admin AI mode
section3.body: When you enable BYOK ("bring your own key") in Settings you provide an API key for a third-party AI provider. The operator stores that key AES-encrypted at rest but does not insulate you from the provider's terms of service or pricing. When you use admin AI mode the operator is paying for your model calls within their configured monthly quota; abuse of that mode is grounds for the operator to disable your account. The operator decides which accounts may use it, and may take that back.

section4.title: Nutrition is not medical advice
section4.body: Every calorie, macro and micronutrient value rendered by the application is computed by a deterministic engine from a curated ingredient database. Values are best-effort and not validated for any medical, clinical or therapeutic purpose. Consult a qualified professional before making dietary changes that affect a medical condition.

section5.title: AI-assisted content
section5.body: AI-drafted recipes, ingredient substitutions and meal swaps carry an ✨ AI-assisted chip. Review them before relying on them. The deterministic engine recomputes nutrition for every AI artefact and rejects nutrition the model invented, but ingredient choices and preparation steps remain AI-authored — sanity-check them against your own dietary needs and health.

section6.title: Curated content licence
section6.body: Curated recipes under data/recipes/ and curated ingredients under data/ingredients.json ship under the repository's licence, the GNU Affero General Public License, version 3. Recipes promoted from user contributions through the curation queue are contributed under the same licence by the act of submission. A recipe the instance's AI writes for you goes to the curation queue by itself, anonymously, and is contributed under the same licence if the curators accept it.

section7.title: Data residency
section7.body: Your data lives in the database of the instance you are using. The upstream project has no access to it, no backups of it, and no recovery path for it. Ask the operator of this instance about backup policy and data handling before storing anything you cannot afford to lose. You can take a copy of everything your account holds, as one file, from the settings at any time.
